title: Engine Fuel — Start Exhaust Gas Temperature Spread Between Engines
abstract: Fault isolation for a wide exhaust gas temperature spread between engines during a cold start, covering the delivery nozzle standard, the fuel temperature and the control unit trim before any engine work.

sections.purpose: This procedure isolates a report of a wide exhaust gas temperature spread between the two engines during start, particularly after a cold soak, and identifies whether the cause is the delivery nozzle, the fuel condition or the control unit.
sections.fault_description: On a cold morning one engine lights later than the other and peaks at a noticeably higher exhaust gas temperature, with a spread of more than sixty degrees between the two. The spread reduces as the day warms and disappears in temperate conditions. Neither engine exceeds a limit, so nothing is recorded automatically, and the report comes from the crew rather than from the system.
sections.isolation_procedure: 1. Record the fuel temperature at the start and the ambient temperature. Below minus twenty degrees at the nozzle the delivered nozzle standard is expected to produce a spread; that is the pattern this procedure addresses. 2. Read the delivery nozzle standard fitted on each engine from the configuration record. A mixed standard across the two engines is the most common cause and is not permitted for more than one hundred flight hours. 3. Read the control unit trim values from both engines and compare against each other and against the build record. 4. Do a fuel sample check for water and for the correct grade at the affected station. 5. Do the delivery nozzle installation check in AMM-M-73-10-11-400-046-A on the engine with the later light-up, including the union torque and the seal condition. 6. If the nozzle standards are mixed, embody the revised nozzle on the remaining engine and repeat the start observation. 7. If both engines carry the revised nozzle and the spread persists, examine the metering unit and the control harness for a signal fault. 8. Do not adjust the control unit trim to compensate for a spread caused by a mixed nozzle standard.
sections.dispatch_note: There is no minimum equipment list item for a start temperature spread, because no limit is exceeded. The condition is dispatchable but must be recorded; a start that exceeds the temperature limit is a separate event and requires an engine inspection before further flight.

type_data.fault_symptom: Exhaust gas temperature spread greater than 60 degrees between engines during a cold start

possible_causes.cause: Delivery nozzle spray pattern collapse at low fuel temperature
Mixed delivery nozzle standard between the two engines
Water in the fuel at the affected station
Engine electronic control unit trim difference

dispatch.dispatch_condition: No limit exceeded. Record the spread and the fuel temperature; a start exceeding the temperature limit requires an engine inspection.
